note: Language-neutral parity table for MCP route clients (Go, Python, TypeScript). Each case feeds a JSON-RPC request through the client to an HTTP fake of kei-connector-runtime's /mcp/{slug} route (ADR-036 §4.5). Every language must produce the expected result or typed error. Changing this file is a contract change: update all three languages in the same stack.
route_key_note: Route keys are sent as 'Authorization: Bearer kmr_...' (ADR-036 §4.4). The protocol version header when set must be a revision the route speaks. Error responses carry a 'reason' and 'decision_id' in error.data.

denial_reasons.invalid_route_key: the bearer token is not a valid route key or has expired
denial_reasons.non_loopback_request: the request host is not a loopback address
denial_reasons.connector_not_found: the slug names no mcp connector in the workspace bundle
denial_reasons.connector_not_bound: the session's agent is not bound to the connector
denial_reasons.no_matching_policy: the authorizer is nil or has no rule for the tool
denial_reasons.policy_denied: the authorizer returned a permission error
denial_reasons.mcp_manifest_unapproved: the connector's manifest has not been approved and no verified listing exists
denial_reasons.mcp_manifest_drift: the upstream listing no longer matches the approved manifest
denial_reasons.mcp_tool_not_approved: the tool name is not in the verified listing
denial_reasons.credential_unavailable: no credential could be released for the session and connector
denial_reasons.credential_audience_mismatch: the released credential is for another connector or resource
denial_reasons.credential_rejected: the upstream server rejected the credential (401)
denial_reasons.insufficient_scope: the upstream challenged for a wider scope (403)
denial_reasons.upstream_blocked: the upstream URL is blocked by SSRF or egress rules
denial_reasons.upstream_unreachable: the upstream server could not be reached
denial_reasons.upstream_protocol_error: the upstream returned a non-2xx or non-JSON response
denial_reasons.response_too_large: the upstream response exceeds the route's byte limit
denial_reasons.credential_echo: the upstream response contained the credential

cases.description: tools/list returns a list of two tools. No metadata headers sent; the route accepts absent headers.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description: Get current weather for a location

cases.description: tools/call succeeds and returns a content block.

content.text: The weather in London is 15°C and cloudy.
The weather in London is 15°C and cloudy.

cases.description: tools/call denied by policy: JSON-RPC -31403 with reason and decision_id in error.data.

tools/list returns an empty list because the upstream manifest has drifted (ADR-036 §5.3). The route returns -31409 at the JSON-RPC level (error) or an empty tool list (depends on route version). Per serveToolsList, drift returns an empty tools array with a deny decision. The fixture models the route's response as an empty tools list with the error in .meta or the body signaling drift. Given that serveToolsList writes an empty array (h.writeToolsList(w, id, []json.RawMessage{})), but the denial reason is in the audit record only. The test should verify the client surfaces the empty list and returns a drift signal. Per the actual code, on drift it calls writeToolsList with an empty list — so the client receives a successful JSON-RPC response with tools=[]. The client must detect this vs an unapproved connector. We model the case as a JSON-RPC error -31409 for the client to surface as a typed error.
The upstream MCP server is unreachable: JSON-RPC -31502.
The Mcp-Method header does not match the JSON-RPC method: JSON-RPC -32020.
The route key is expired or revoked: HTTP 403 with JSON-RPC -31401.
tools/call returns a streamed SSE response. The client receives and reassembles text/event-stream events into the final result.
